transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-21 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Janelle Ortiz (Redwood SE), Alex Wu (Redwood Solutions), Rajiv Menon (Polaris Crest CTO), Maya Torres (Head of Platform), Evan Li (Infra), Hank (Procurement - partial)

--- Optional auto sections present below ---
Summary: quick intro, map constraints, define pilot scope and next steps (see action items)
Topics: see metadata tag list above
Action items: see metadata field above

--- Transcript body (auto) ---
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes, wanted to give a quick intro from our side and then hear the Polaris Crest goals and where you see a reseller / managed-onramp fit.
[00:22] Rajiv (Polaris Crest - CTO): Thanks Samir, appreciate it. We're looking to add a managed inference offering that our channel partners can resell. Key things for us are predictable latency for interactive apps, easy region controls for customers, and a simple way to bundle costs.
[00:40] Maya (Head of Platform): Yup, and compliance is big — many of our customers require SOC2 and key-management controls, plus audit trails for model inputs. We also want the ability to offer both fully-hosted and private-VPC variants.
[00:58] Janelle (Redwood SE): Totally, that's exactly what Redwood's Dedicated and Private modes aim for. Quick question on expected workload — latency SLOs and QPS patterns?
[01:12] Maya (Head of Platform): Mostly conversational features, median P95 target of ~220-300ms for 512 tokens, bursts up to 400 qps for some enterprise accounts. We can shave some latency at higher cost but need to understand tradeoffs.
[01:31] Alex (Redwood Solutions): When you say 220–300ms, that’s end-to-end from app to response? or just token-generation?
[01:36] Evan (Infra Eng): App-to-response including our edge routing and a small L7 proxy. We're trying to keep headroom for network hops.
[01:45] Samir (Redwood AE): Good detail — that helps. On routing, Redwood supports policy-based smart routing so you can route production traffic to Dedicated pools, and fallback to cheaper hosted variants during capacity pressure.
[01:59] Rajiv: How well does the fallback preserve response characteristics? We can't have large quality regressions when we fail over.
[02:09] Janelle (Redwood SE): Right, we do model-variant mapping — you can pin a primary model and define acceptable fallbacks. We also do canary rollouts and A/B for that so you can measure regression. That said, fallback may change tokenization/latent behaviors; we recommend an eval suite.
[02:29] (Speaker 3): mhm, and we have prefix KV cache support to reduce repeated context costs — helpful for chat sessions.
[02:36] Maya: Could you spell that, K V cache, I sometimes see it as K V cash in old notes.
[02:41] Janelle: Yeah, it's KV cache — we cache key/value attention states between requests to avoid recomputing for overlapping prefixes. That lowers per-token computation and can help P95 for sessiony workloads.
[02:55] Rajiv: Any constraints on private deploys? We need to do VPC peering for certain customers and have HSM/KMS integrations.
[03:06] Janelle: For Private we have a customer-controlled control plane with optional on-prem components. KMS/HSM integration is supported — we integrate with major KMS providers and can also accept bring-your-own HSM hooks, though the on-prem packaging needs some ops coordination.
[03:20] Evan: Do you support per-tenant RBAC? Audit logs?
[03:24] Alex: Yes, RBAC scoped to routes and models, and audit logs stream to your SIEM (or we can ship them to S3 with retention controls).
[03:33] Rajiv: From a reseller POV, are there reseller APIs for provisioning and billing? We don't want to be manual.
[03:40] Samir: Good question — we offer partner APIs and a program for reseller billing so you can have consolidated invoices or per-customer breakouts. The reseller flow is straightforward but we need to align on SLAs and support levels.
[03:56] Maya: On hardware side — we're considering both A10-level instances for cost and H100-equivalents for low-latency/high-throughput customers. Any guidance?
[04:07] Janelle: A10-like configs are good for many embedding and smaller gen use-cases; for conversational P95 in the 220ms range at 512 tokens, you typically need H-class GPUs or well-optimized quantized runtimes and aggressive batching. We can share quantization guidance and kernel selection notes.
[04:27] Rajiv: Do you do quantized model variants for fallbacks? How much quality hit should we expect?
[04:33] Janelle: We support quantized variants and usually recommend a specific profile for each model and sequence length. Quality drop varies by model — we'll recommend an eval harness to establish acceptable thresholds.
[04:47] (Background: brief crosstalk)
[04:50] Hank (Procurement): Quick procurement note — reseller margins, lead times for reserved capacity are important. We'll want a template for minimum commitment levels.
[04:58] Samir: We can provide a template term sheet. For Dedicated reserved capacity we do monthly/annual commits; there are commit tiers that change pricing.
[05:08] Rajiv: Sandbox / pilot — we want to run an end-to-end test that exercises routing, fallback, and measures latency and cost per token. What's the easiest path?
[05:18] Samir: We'll provision a sandbox account scoped to Polaris Crest with a small Dedicated pool + hosted fallbacks. Janelle will put together a tiny benchmark script you can run from your side to simulate 50-400 QPS with session affinity.
[05:31] Janelle: I'll also include a sample prompt set and automated eval so you can spot regression when fallbacks trigger.
[05:38] Maya: Great. Also need security docs — encryption at rest, SSO, audit logs for the pilot.
[05:44] Samir: I'll attach our SOC2 pack, SSO/SAML integration spec and the audit log schema.
[05:50] Rajiv: For region controls, can you restrict which models are served in which regions? We have European customers with data residency needs.
[05:57] Janelle: Yes — routing policies can be geography-bound and you can pin model versions by region. For stricter needs we recommend Private deployments in-region.
[06:07] Evan: One trick — our proxy adds ~30ms. If Redwood’s P95 is 200ms token gen, we need total under 300 including proxy. Can you help with continuous batching knobs?
[06:19] Janelle: We expose batching windows and max tokens per batch and can tune for latency vs throughput. There's also automatic adaptive batching we can enable. We can run a small experiment with your proxy in the loop.
[06:31] Rajiv: How about observability? We need per-route token breakdown, cost per request, and traces.
[06:38] Alex: Redwood Console gives per-route and token-level cost, latency heatmaps, and tracing hooks you can attach to your APM. We can give a short walkthrough during the demo.
[06:48] Maya: Any legal obligations on data retention for resold customers? Customers may require deletion on request.
[06:54] Samir: We support configurable retention and can add obligations into the reseller agreement. For hosted we retain transient fields by default but can toggle retention on a per-tenant basis for compliance.
[07:06] (Speaker label glitch - 'Speaker 2' shows briefly)
[07:10] Speaker 2: there was a question about model catalog — do you host open models only or also provide closed / third-party models?
[07:17] Janelle: We have a model catalog with open models and some licensed model variants. For third-party closed models we have partner arrangements but terms vary. If you have preferred models we can discuss onboarding.
[07:29] Rajiv: We might want to onboard partner-tuned models later. For the pilot let's keep to verified open models for easier licensing.
[07:36] Samir: Makes sense. We'll pick a couple of Redwood-verified models for the pilot and show fallback variants.
[07:43] Evan: Quick note on KV cache behavior — do you shard caches across GPUs or is it node-local? We worry about cache invalidation across failover.
[07:53] Janelle: KV cache is per-serving instance; for high-availability we do asynchronous replication and graceful migration on failover. Some edge cases can cause cold-starts; our routing policies can prefer warm pools for session-heavy customers.
[08:09] Rajiv: That replication detail matters for session stickiness and cost.
[08:14] Samir: We'll include KV behavior docs in the sandbox packet.
[08:19] Maya: On billing, can we get a cost model example for a reseller — per-token rates, markups, and reserved capacity amortization?
[08:28] Samir: Yes — I'll send an example spreadsheet showing different pricing levers (per-token hosted, dedicated amortized cost, burst pricing) and a sample reseller margin model.
[08:39] Hank: Procurement will need a standard SLA clause and RTO/RPO expectations for Dedicated.
[08:44] Alex: We'll share standard SLA language and SLA tiers for Dedicated vs Hosted; Dedicated has uptime SLAs and latency SLO guidance.
[08:53] (Small pause)
[08:57] Rajiv: Ok, high-level pilot scope: 2-week sandbox, dedicated small pool in us-west and eu-west, hosted fallbacks, run the benchmark script at 50–200 QPS, collect P95, cost per 1k tokens, and regression reports. Is that feasible?
[09:12] Janelle: Yep that's doable. We'll need your NFR doc with exact QPS shape and sample prompts.
[09:18] Maya: We'll share that today.
[09:20] Samir: Great — after the sandbox we'll regroup and, if the pilot meets thresholds, we can scope a reserved capacity demo and term sheet.
[09:28] Rajiv: Any potential blockers from your side for a reseller integration?
[09:33] Alex: The main stat is contract terms around support and whether you want us to white-label the console. White-labeling is possible but requires extra integration.
[09:43] Evan: Also network & VPC peering has usual ops tasks. We'll need a runbook.
[09:48] Janelle: We'll provide an ops runbook for peering and firewall rules.
[09:52] Samir: Cool. Anything else from Polaris Crest?
[09:55] Maya: Nothing else. We'll fill in the NFR doc and expect the security pack.
[09:59] Rajiv: Thanks all.
[10:01] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up with the packet and sandbox creds.
[10:05] (call wraps, brief goodbyes)

--- End of transcript ---

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels (Speaker 2/3) and minor word swaps (K V cash vs KV cache). Natural speech patterns preserved, short crosstalk fragments included.
